title: Rehoboam
lead: Solomon's son and successor, king of Judah for seventeen years (about 930–913 BC). His harsh answer at Shechem split the kingdom, and in his fifth year Shishak of Egypt invaded Judah.

sections.b: Rehoboam went to Shechem to be made king, refused the northern tribes' request to lighten Solomon's yoke, and lost ten tribes to Jeroboam (1 Kings 12:1–20). The prophet Shemaiah stopped him from making war on the north (1 Kings 12:21–24). Kings says Judah built high places, standing stones and Asherah poles in his reign, and that Shishak took the treasures of the temple and palace, including Solomon's gold shields (1 Kings 14:21–28). His mother was Naamah the Ammonite, one of Solomon's foreign wives (1 Kings 14:21).
